committee_notes:
Committee Notes

The Supreme Court, in the case of

State ex rel. Gray v. Jensen, (Mo. 1965), 395 S.W.2d 143, in discussing Committee Notes, stated: "Our Rules of Civil Procedure were adopted by this court on August 10, 1959, to become effective April 1, 1960. This court had appointed one committee which drafted proposed rules which were then submitted to the bench and bar of the state for comment. Thereafter, this court appointed another committee to revise the proposed rules in the light of the comments and suggestions received. It was the draft of this latter committee which was approved and adopted by the court. The rules as thus drafted and submitted by the committee were accompanied by committee notes following each rule. These were explanatory in nature, giving information as to the source of the proposed rule, any changes made from the language of the statute or rule from which taken, and other explanatory comments. These committee notes are comparable to legislative committee reports which pertain to legislation which is passed and are to be considered in determining the scope and meaning of the rule under consideration, just as the legislative committee reports are considered in construing the legislative enactments."

norms.heading: Rules – When Applicable

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rule 41

norms.text:
(1) Civil actions pending in this Court and court of appeals;

(2) Civil actions pending before a circuit judge except those actions governed by the probate code;

(3) Civil actions pending before an associate circuit judge sitting as a circuit judge.
(b) Rules 41, 54.18, 55.03, 56, 57, 58, 59, 60, 61, 62, and 67.03 apply to proceedings in the probate division of the circuit court. The judge of the probate division may order that any or all of the other Rules 41 through 101 or specified subdivisions of the rules shall be applicable in a particular matter. Any such order shall specify the rules or subdivisions to be applied and a time for compliance with the order. The order shall be served upon all of the parties.
(c) The transfer of an action from the probate division to the circuit division shall not make subdivisions of Rule 55, except Rule 55.03, applicable unless ordered by the circuit division. Any such order shall specify the subdivisions of Rule 55 to be applied and a time for compliance with the order. The order shall be served upon all of the parties.
(d) Civil actions pending in the associate circuit division shall be governed by Rules 41 through 101 except where otherwise provided by law. No such law shall affect the application of Rule 55.03 or 55.22. When portions of Rule 55 do not apply to an action originally filed in the associate circuit division, the subsequent transfer of the action to the circuit division shall not make those portions of Rule 55 applicable unless ordered by the circuit division. Any such order shall specify the subdivisions of Rule 55 to be applied and a time for compliance with the order. The order shall be served upon all of the parties.
(e) Rule 103 and Court Operating Rule 27 shall apply to all matters subject to electronic filing. To the extent there is a conflict between Rule 103 and Rules 41 through 101, Rule 103 shall apply.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 749 étend les dispositions du livre à toutes les juridictions judiciaires statuant en matière civile, sous réserve des règles spéciales. Le RSMo 506.010 et la Rule 41.01 définissent également l’application générale de la procédure civile, mais selon les catégories de tribunaux et les exclusions propres au Missouri.
correspondences.note_en: Article 749 makes the book applicable before all courts of the judicial order in civil matters, subject to special rules. RSMo 506.010 and Rule 41.01 likewise establish broad civil-procedure coverage, but use Missouri-specific court categories and exclusions.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose l’application des règles du titre lorsque le tribunal judiciaire statue en matière commerciale. La Rule 41.01 détermine les actions et divisions auxquelles les règles civiles s’appliquent, tandis que la Rule 41.04 prévoit une procédure subsidiaire cohérente avec les textes applicables.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires the title’s procedural rules to govern when a judicial court hears a commercial matter. Rule 41.01 specifies when the civil rules apply in various courts and divisions, while Rule 41.04 supplies a consistent procedure when no specific rule exists.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article désigne le président du tribunal judiciaire et impose une procédure particulière pour certaines demandes successorales, notamment dans un partage amiable. Les règles 96.01 et 96.32 organisent la partition de biens immobiliers ou mobiliers, tandis que la règle 41.01 encadre l’application des règles civiles en matière successorale; aucune ne reproduit la compétence ni la procédure française.
correspondences.note_en: The article assigns specified succession applications to the president of the judicial court and prescribes a particular procedure, including for amicable partition. Rules 96.01 and 96.32 govern partition of real or personal property, while Rule 41.01 addresses civil-rule applicability in probate proceedings; none reproduces the French jurisdiction or procedure.

norms.heading: Signatures of Judicial Officers and Court Officials

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rule 41

norms.text:
(a) Signature of judicial officer. Documents requiring a judge's or commissioner's signature may be signed by an original signature, stamped signature, or an electronic graphic representation of a signature. When the signature appears on a docket sheet entry, the entry may be signed in the following manner: /s/ John or Jane Judge.

(b) Signature of clerk. Documents requiring a clerk's signature may be signed by an original signature, stamped signature, an electronic graphic representation of a signature, or /s/ John or Jane Clerk.
(c) Signature of court reporter and transcriber. Documents requiring a court reporter's or transcriber's signature may be signed by an original signature, stamped signature, an electronic graphic representation of a signature, or /s/ John or Jane Person.

correspondences.note_fr: RSMo 513.390 concerne, dans une procédure particulière, les dépositions écrites d’une partie qui témoigne sous serment et exige leur souscription ainsi qu’un jurat. La Rule 41.08 régit les signatures du juge et du greffier, sans prévoir les formalités de lecture, de certification, de refus ou de datation de l’article.
correspondences.note_en: RSMo 513.390 concerns, in a specific proceeding, written evidence of a party testifying under oath and requires subscription and a jurat. Rule 41.08 governs judge and clerk signatures but not the article’s reading, certification, refusal, or dating formalities.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose la signature du président et du greffier, prévoit le remplacement du président empêché et encadre la signature électronique qualifiée du jugement, avec une sanction de vice de forme. Les règles du Missouri reconnaissent les signatures du juge et du greffier, ainsi que les signatures électroniques, mais sans reprendre ces conditions ni cette sanction.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires signatures by the presiding judge and clerk, addresses an unavailable presiding judge, and regulates qualified electronic signatures, with a formal defect sanction. Missouri recognizes judge and clerk signatures and electronic signatures, but does not reproduce these conditions or sanction.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose la signature de l’arrêt par le président, les rapporteurs et le greffier. La Rule 41.08 règle les modalités de signature des magistrats et du greffier, tandis que la Rule 74.01 exige la signature du juge pour un jugement, sans imposer cette combinaison de signatures.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires the judgment to be signed by the president, reporting judge(s), and clerk. Rule 41.08 governs how judicial officers and clerks sign, and Rule 74.01 requires a judge’s signature for a judgment, but neither requires this specific combination of signatures.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article impose la signature du président, du rapporteur et du greffier, ainsi que la transmission de la décision à la juridiction d'origine. La Rule 41.08 encadre les modalités de signature, tandis que la Rule 84.28 permet le renvoi de la cause avec la décision, sans imposer ces formalités précises.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires signatures by the president, reporting judge, and clerk, and transmission of the decision to the originating court. Rule 41.08 governs signature methods, while Rule 84.28 permits remand with the decision, without imposing these precise formalities.

norms.heading: Service of Pleadings and Other Papers

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 43 — Service and Filing of Pleadings and Papers

norms.text:
(a) Service – When Required. Each party shall be served with:

(1) Every pleading subsequent to the original petition;

(2) Every written motion, other than one that may be heard

ex parte; and

(3) Every written notice, appearance, demand, offer of judgment, order, and similar paper that by statute, court rule or order is required to be served.
No service need be made on parties in default for failure to appear, except that pleadings asserting new or additional claims for relief against them shall be served upon them in the manner provided for service of summons. In cases filed under chapter 517, RSMo, service as required in Rule 43.01 shall be made on every party that has entered or appeared in person or by attorney.
(b) Service – On Whom. Whenever under these rules or any of the statutes of this state service is required or permitted to be made upon a party represented by an attorney of record, the service shall be made upon the attorney, unless the court orders service upon the party. When more than one attorney represents a party, service may be made upon any such attorney. If an attorney has filed an entry of limited appearance for an otherwise self-represented person, service shall be made on:
(1) The self-represented person, and

(2) Until the attorney files a termination of limited appearance, the attorney.

(c) Service – How and by Whom Made. Attorneys and self-represented parties shall state in the signature blocks of their pleadings their current mailing addresses, telephone numbers, facsimile numbers, electronic addresses, and Missouri bar numbers if any. This information shall be kept current at all times. Service may be directed to any of these addresses.
Unless otherwise ordered by the court, service required by Rules 43.01(a) and 43.01(b) may be made in the following manner:

(1) Upon the attorney:

(A) By delivering a copy to the attorney;

(B) By leaving a copy at the attorney’s office with a clerk, receptionist, or secretary or with an attorney employed by or associated with the attorney to be served;
(C) By facsimile transmission;

(D) By electronic mail; or

(E) By mailing a copy to the attorney at the attorney’s last known address;

(2) Upon a party:

(A) By delivering or mailing a copy to the party;

(B) By facsimile transmission;

(C) By electronic mail; or
(D) By serving a copy in the manner provided for service of summons in Rule 54.13.

(d) Service – When Complete. Personal service on attorneys and self-represented parties and service by leaving a copy at the attorney’s office is complete upon delivery.

Service by mail is complete upon mailing.

Service by facsimile transmission or electronic mail is complete upon transmission, except that a transmission made on a Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday, or after 5:00 p.m. shall be complete on the next day that is not a Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday.
(e) Service – How Shown. Service may be shown by acknowledgment of receipt or by written certificate of the person making such service. Certificates of service shall state the:

(1) Name of each person served;

(2) Date of service;

(3) Method of service; and

(4) Address of service, such as mailing address, facsimile number or electronic mail address.
(f) Service – Numerous Defendants. If there are unusually large numbers of defendants in an action, the court, upon motion or of its own initiative, may order that:

(1) Service of the pleadings of the defendants, and reply thereto, need not be made as between the defendants;

(2) Any cross-claim, counterclaim, or pleading constituting an avoidance or affirmative defense contained therein shall be deemed to be denied or avoided by all other parties; and
(3) The filing of any such pleading and service thereof upon the plaintiff constitutes due notice of it to the parties.

A copy of every such order shall be served upon the parties in such manner and form as the court directs.

(g) Service – Time for – When No Time Specified. When provision is made for the time of filing papers and none is made for the time of service thereof, copies shall be served on the day of filing or as soon thereafter as can be done.
(h) Service of Orders, Judgments and Other Documents. Any order, judgment or other document issued by the court may be transmitted to the attorney or party as authorized in Rule 43.01(c), provided service pursuant to Rule 54 is not required. Such documents may be transmitted to non-parties in the same manner as is authorized for service upon an attorney.
