correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose une mention spéciale sur le mémoire de QPC et organise, dans le pourvoi, la réponse des autres parties dans un délai d’un mois selon les règles du pourvoi. Rule 84.05 règle les délais des mémoires d’appel et Rule 43.02 le dépôt des actes, sans prévoir la mention ni le régime particulier de la QPC.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires a special designation on the constitutional-question memorandum and sets a one-month response period for other parties under appeal-filing rules. Rule 84.05 governs appellate brief deadlines and Rule 43.02 governs filing, but neither provides the special designation or constitutional-question procedure.

correspondences.note_fr: Rule 63.01 traite de la fixation des affaires civiles pour l'audience, et Rule 43.02 du dépôt des actes au tribunal. Aucun de ces textes ne prévoit la convention participative, l'information spécifique du juge ni le mécanisme de clôture de l'instruction.
correspondences.note_en: Rule 63.01 addresses setting civil actions for trial, and Rule 43.02 addresses filing papers with the court. Neither provides for the participatory agreement, specific notice to the judge, or the case-preparation closure mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose une inscription de faux écrite, précise, déposée en double au greffe, puis dénoncée au défendeur dans le mois. Les règles du Missouri encadrent les motions écrites et motivées, leur dépôt au greffe et leur notification, mais ne prévoient ni l’inscription de faux ni ses formalités spéciales.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires a written, particularized forgery claim, filed in duplicate with the clerk and served within one month. Missouri rules govern written, particularized motions, filing with the clerk, and service, but do not provide the special mechanism or formalities of an incidental forgery claim.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose la signature du président et du greffier, prévoit le remplacement du président empêché et encadre la signature électronique qualifiée du jugement, avec une sanction de vice de forme. Les règles du Missouri reconnaissent les signatures du juge et du greffier, ainsi que les signatures électroniques, mais sans reprendre ces conditions ni cette sanction.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires signatures by the presiding judge and clerk, addresses an unavailable presiding judge, and regulates qualified electronic signatures, with a formal defect sanction. Missouri recognizes judge and clerk signatures and electronic signatures, but does not reproduce these conditions or sanction.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article organise un dossier individuel contenant les actes, documents, décisions, représentants et, en procédure orale, les prétentions des parties. Les règles du Missouri prévoient le dépôt des actes, l'apparition des avocats, le dossier d'appel et l'inscription des jugements, mais non un dossier de greffe identique ni la consignation générale des prétentions orales.
correspondences.note_en: The article establishes an individual case file containing documents, decisions, representatives, and oral claims. Missouri rules address filing papers, counsel appearances, appellate records, and judgment entries, but do not provide an identical clerk-maintained file or a general record of oral claims.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article autorise la transmission électronique des actes, pièces, avis, convocations, rapports, procès-verbaux et décisions, sous réserve des modalités du titre ou de règles spéciales. Les règles du Missouri organisent surtout le dépôt électronique et la signification électronique, sans couvrir l’ensemble de ces actes ni selon un régime unique.
correspondences.note_en: The article authorizes electronic transmission of procedural documents, exhibits, notices, summonses, reports, records, and enforceable copies, subject to the Title’s modalities or special rules. The Missouri provisions mainly regulate electronic filing and electronic service, without covering all listed documents under a single regime.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article prévoit un avis électronique de réception ou de mise à disposition indiquant la date et, le cas échéant, l’heure, qui remplace visa, cachet et signature et dispense de certains exemplaires matériels. Le Missouri reconnaît la notification générée par le système, fixe l’achèvement de la transmission électronique et assimile la signature électronique à l’original, mais sans reprendre exactement ces effets.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires an electronic acknowledgment of receipt or availability stating the date and, where applicable, time; it substitutes for required receipt formalities and eliminates certain paper-copy requirements. Missouri recognizes system-generated notice, defines completion of electronic transmission, and gives electronic signatures the effect of originals, but does not reproduce the same rule in full.

correspondences.note_fr: Les dispositifs électroniques doivent assurer l’identification, l’intégrité, la sécurité, la confidentialité, la conservation et la preuve des dates, et l’identification peut valoir signature. Les Rules 43.01 et 43.02 règlent respectivement le service, le moment de sa réalisation, le dépôt électronique, l’effet du dépôt et la conservation de l’original signé. La Rule 84.026 organise le service électronique dans les juridictions d’appel, sans reprendre toutes les garanties techniques.
correspondences.note_en: Electronic systems must ensure identification, integrity, security, confidentiality, preservation, and proof of dates, and identification may constitute a signature. Rules 43.01 and 43.02 address service timing, electronic filing, filing effects, and retention of the signed filing. Rule 84.026 organizes electronic service in appellate courts without matching all technical safeguards.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 756 règle la saisine du tribunal par remise ou transmission de la requête, y compris par voie électronique et, dans un cas particulier, par le conciliateur. Les règles 53.01 et 506.110 prévoient l’introduction par dépôt d’une petition, tandis que la règle 43.02(c) admet certains dépôts électroniques, sans reprendre toutes les modalités françaises.
correspondences.note_en: Article 756 governs commencing an action by filing a petition, including electronic filing and transmission by a conciliator in a specific situation. Rules 53.01 and RSMo 506.110 provide commencement by filing a petition, while Rule 43.02(c) permits certain electronic filings, but Missouri does not reproduce all French procedures.

frcp.evidence: Committee Note – 1974 This is the same as Rule 3 of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 764 prévoit l’information de l’avocat du demandeur, la remise d’une copie de la constitution au greffe et, éventuellement, le consentement à une procédure sans audience. Les Rules 55.035, 43.01 et 43.02 couvrent respectivement l’entrée en scène, la notification et le dépôt, sans reprendre toutes ces exigences ni le consentement spécifique.
correspondences.note_en: Article 764 requires notice to opposing counsel, filing a copy of the appearance with the clerk, and possibly consent to a proceeding without a hearing. Rules 55.035, 43.01, and 43.02 cover appearance, service, and filing, but not all of these requirements or the specific consent.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 767 organise la remise au greffe de l’acte de constitution et des conclusions, selon leur notification et le moment de la saisine. Les Rules 43.02 et 55.035 couvrent respectivement le dépôt et l’apparence de l’avocat; RSMo 506.100 prévoit aussi le dépôt après notification, mais sans le même mécanisme.
correspondences.note_en: Article 767 governs filing the appearance and conclusions with the clerk, keyed to service and commencement. Rules 43.02 and 55.035 address filing and attorney appearance, and RSMo 506.100 also addresses post-service filing, but none has the same complete mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 769 prévoit la remise d’une copie au greffe, la constatation de la date par le greffier et la restitution immédiate de l’original. La Rule 43.02 assimile le dépôt au greffe à la remise au clerk et prévoit la mention de la date dans certains cas, mais ne reprend pas l’ensemble de ces formalités.
correspondences.note_en: Article 769 requires filing a copy with the clerk, recording the filing date, and immediately returning the original. Rule 43.02 treats filing with the clerk as filing with the court and allows the filing date to be noted in certain cases, but does not reproduce all of these formalities; Rule 41.08 concerns clerk signatures.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article organise le dépôt au greffe de copies de la requête, des pièces et de l’ordonnance, ainsi que la restitution de copies lorsque l’assignation n’est pas déposée. La Rule 43.02 régit le dépôt des actes auprès du greffier, mais ne prévoit pas ces modalités particulières de constitution et de restitution du dossier.
correspondences.note_en: The article governs filing copies of the application, exhibits, and order with the clerk, and their return if the summons is not filed. Rule 43.02 governs filing papers with the clerk, but does not provide these specific dossier and return procedures.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article permet, avec l’accord exprès des parties, une procédure sans audience fondée sur des écritures et pièces, avec échanges et calendrier fixés par le juge. La Rule 55.30(c) permet une décision sans plaidoirie orale, tandis que les Rules 43.01 et 43.02 régissent la notification et le dépôt des écritures, sans reprendre ce régime complet.
correspondences.note_en: The article allows, with express party agreement, proceedings without a hearing based on written submissions and exhibits, under a judicial timetable. Rule 55.30(c) permits submission without oral argument, while Rules 43.01 and 43.02 govern service and filing but do not replicate the complete procedure.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 829 encadre le consentement écrit de toutes les parties à une procédure sans audience et impose des mentions d’identité, une signature manuscrite et un justificatif officiel. Les règles 55.30, 55.03 et 43.02 prévoient respectivement la soumission sans audience, la signature des actes et la signature électronique, sans reprendre ces exigences cumulatives d’identité.
correspondences.note_en: Article 829 regulates the parties’ written consent to proceed without a hearing and requires detailed identity information, a handwritten signature, and official proof of identity. Rules 55.30, 55.03, and 43.02 address submission without oral hearing, filing signatures, and electronic signatures, but do not impose the same identity requirements.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 832 encadre une demande incidente de délai de paiement formée par courrier au greffe, avec communication des pièces et possibilité d’absence à l’audience. Les Rules 55.26, 43.01, 43.02 et 44.01 traitent respectivement de la forme des motions, de leur notification, du dépôt et du délai de notification, mais ne reproduisent pas ce régime particulier.
correspondences.note_en: Article 832 governs an incidental payment-time request filed by letter with the clerk, including transmission of supporting documents and the applicant’s possible nonappearance. Rules 55.26, 43.01, 43.02, and 44.01 address motion form, service, filing, and notice timing, but do not replicate this specific procedure.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article règle la saisine par remise de l’assignation, la caducité en cas de remise tardive et une procédure écrite sans audience organisée par le président. Les règles du Missouri prévoient le commencement par dépôt, le dépôt des actes, la soumission écrite de certaines demandes et la notification entre parties, mais sans régime identique de caducité ni de procédure au fond sans audience.
correspondences.note_en: The article governs commencement by filing the summons, nullity for late filing, and a written procedure without an oral hearing organized by the chamber president. Missouri rules cover commencement by filing, filing papers, written submission of certain matters, and service, but do not provide the same nullity mechanism or full written merits procedure.

frcp.evidence: Committee Note – 1974 This is the same as Rule 3 of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 846 règle les modalités de présentation de la requête, notamment la qualité du présentateur et son dépôt au greffe. La Rule 43.02 encadre le dépôt des actes auprès du greffier, tandis que les Rules 84.24 et 90.02 prévoient des modalités comparables pour certaines requêtes ou demandes spécialisées.
correspondences.note_en: Article 846 governs how a petition is presented, including who may submit it and filing with the clerk. Rule 43.02 regulates filing with the clerk, while Rules 84.24 and 90.02 provide comparable filing mechanisms for particular petitions or applications.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 850 impose, sous peine d’irrecevabilité, la transmission électronique de certains actes et prévoit un support papier en cas d’impossibilité, ainsi que la remise électronique des avis aux avocats. La Rule 43.02 encadre le dépôt et autorise le dépôt électronique par règle locale, tandis que la Rule 43.01 organise la notification électronique, sans reprendre le même caractère obligatoire ni toutes les exceptions.
correspondences.note_en: Article 850 mandates electronic filing for specified proceedings, provides paper alternatives when electronic transmission is impossible, and requires electronic delivery of notices to counsel. Rule 43.02 governs filing and permits electronic filing by local rule, while Rule 43.01 governs electronic service, but neither reproduces the same mandatory scheme or all exceptions.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article fait dépendre la saisine du tribunal de la remise au greffe d’une copie de l’assignation, au plus tard huit jours avant l’audience, sous peine de caducité. Les règles du Missouri rattachent plutôt le commencement au dépôt de la petition et encadrent le dépôt des actes, sans reprendre cette exigence de délai ou cette sanction.
correspondences.note_en: The article makes court seisin depend on filing a copy of the summons with the clerk no later than eight days before the hearing, subject to lapse. Missouri rules instead link commencement to filing the petition and regulate filing of papers, without reproducing that deadline or sanction.

frcp.evidence: Committee Note – 1974 This is the same as Rule 3 of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure

correspondences.note_fr: L’article dispose que le tribunal est saisi par la remise de la requête conjointe. La Rule 53.01 rattache le commencement de l’action au dépôt de la petition, et la Rule 43.02 précise que le dépôt s’effectue auprès du greffier; RSMo 506.110 confirme l’effet introductif du dépôt.
correspondences.note_en: The article provides that the court is seized by delivery of the joint petition. Rule 53.01 makes filing a petition the commencement of the action, while Rule 43.02 specifies filing with the clerk; RSMo 506.110 likewise gives filing the effect of commencing suit.

frcp.evidence: Committee Note – 1974 This is the same as Rule 3 of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure

correspondences.note_fr: L’article définit les conclusions d’appel recevables par leur dépôt au greffe, leur notification dans les délais et leur fonction de détermination de l’objet du litige. Les Rules 84.04 et 84.05 encadrent le contenu et les délais des mémoires, tandis que les Rules 43.01 et 43.02 régissent leur notification et leur dépôt.
correspondences.note_en: The article defines appellate submissions by their filing with the clerk, timely service, and role in determining the dispute. Rules 84.04 and 84.05 regulate brief contents and deadlines, while Rules 43.01 and 43.02 govern service and filing.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose la notification simultanée des conclusions et pièces, le dépôt d’une copie au greffe avec preuve de notification et l’irrecevabilité des pièces soutenant des conclusions irrecevables. Les règles du Missouri organisent la notification, le dépôt et le dépôt des pièces, sans prévoir cette simultanéité ni cette sanction spécifique.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires simultaneous service of briefs and exhibits, filing a copy with proof of service, and inadmissibility of exhibits supporting inadmissible briefs. Missouri rules address service, filing, and appellate exhibits, but not the same simultaneity or sanction.

correspondences.note_fr: La cour est saisie par le dépôt d’une copie de l’assignation avant l’audience, sous peine de caducité constatée d’office. La Rule 81.04 régit le dépôt de l’avis d’appel, la Rule 84.08 la sanction du défaut de poursuivre l’appel, et la Rule 43.02 le dépôt des actes, mais aucune ne reprend exactement ce mécanisme.
correspondences.note_en: The appellate court is seized by filing a copy of the summons before the hearing, with ex officio dismissal for late filing. Rule 81.04 governs filing the notice of appeal, Rule 84.08 sanctions failures to pursue an appeal, and Rule 43.02 governs filing papers, but none matches the mechanism exactly.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article 962 règle le moment du dépôt au greffe de la constitution et des conclusions, en le liant à leur notification ou à la remise de la déclaration. La Rule 43.02 et le RSMo 506.100 imposent également le dépôt auprès du greffe avant ou après la notification, mais sans cette articulation propre à l'appel français.
correspondences.note_en: Article 962 governs when the appearance and conclusions must be filed with the clerk, tying filing to service or to delivery of the notice of appeal. Rule 43.02 and RSMo 506.100 likewise require filing before service or within five days afterward, but do not contain the same French appellate-specific timing.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 966 règle la remise d’une copie au greffe, la constatation de la date par le greffier et la restitution immédiate de l’original. La Rule 43.02 et la Rule 81.04 reconnaissent le dépôt auprès du greffe et sa date, mais ne prévoient pas exactement cette formalité de visa et de restitution.
correspondences.note_en: Article 966 governs filing a copy with the clerk, recording the filing date, and immediately returning the original. Rule 43.02 and Rule 81.04 address filing with the clerk and the filing date, but do not replicate the precise endorsement-and-return procedure.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose au pourvoi incident la forme d’un mémoire, des indications déterminées, des délais de dépôt et de notification, ainsi qu’un mémoire en réponse. Les Rules 84.05 et 84.04 concernent les délais et le contenu des briefs, tandis que les Rules 43.01 et 43.02 régissent leur signification et leur dépôt, sans mécanisme identique de pourvoi incident.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires an incidental appeal to take the form of a memorandum, with specified contents, filing and service deadlines, and a response memorandum. Rules 84.05 and 84.04 address brief deadlines and contents, while Rules 43.01 and 43.02 govern service and filing, but none creates the same incidental-appeal mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1145 règle la signature conjointe de la convention de divorce, le nombre d’originaux, les annexes et certaines transmissions. RSMo 452.325 reconnaît les accords écrits de séparation et leur force dans le jugement, tandis que Rule 43.02(c) traite seulement de la signature et du dépôt électroniques.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1145 governs joint execution of the divorce agreement, originals, annexes, and certain transmissions. RSMo 452.325 recognizes written separation agreements and their effect in the decree, while Rule 43.02(c) addresses only electronic filing and signatures.

correspondences.note_fr: Les Rules 43.02 et 43.01 couvrent respectivement le dépôt auprès du greffe et, de manière générale, la transmission de documents par remise ou courrier. Elles ne reprennent pas les règles spéciales du mandat, la compétence, le contenu de la requête ni la procédure d’audience.
correspondences.note_en: Rules 43.02 and 43.01 respectively address filing with the clerk and, generally, delivery or mailing of documents. They do not reproduce the mandate-specific rules, jurisdiction, petition contents, or hearing procedure.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1334 fixe le contenu et les modalités de dépôt, d’inscription et de consultation de la déclaration d’acceptation à concurrence de l’actif net. La Rule 43.02 régit la remise et le dépôt des actes auprès du greffe, mais ne prévoit ni cette déclaration successorale ni son registre particulier.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1334 specifies the contents and filing, registration, and inspection of an acceptance declaration limiting liability to net assets. Rule 43.02 governs filing papers with the clerk, but does not provide for this succession declaration or its specialized register.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article impose à l'héritier ou au notaire de déposer au greffe le compte de l'administration successorale après le règlement ou l'épuisement de l'actif, avec publicité. La Rule 43.02 régit le dépôt auprès du greffier, tandis que RSMo 515.655 prévoit le dépôt d'un compte par un receiver, sans publicité successorale.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires the heir or notary to file the estate-administration account with the clerk after creditors are paid or assets exhausted, with publication. Rule 43.02 governs filing with the clerk, while RSMo 515.655 requires a receiver's accounting but does not provide for this succession-specific publication.

correspondences.note_fr: La Rule 43.02 régit le dépôt auprès du greffe, mais ne prévoit ni la conservation comme minute, ni la remise d'une copie revêtue de la formule exécutoire, ni la restitution des pièces.
correspondences.note_en: Rule 43.02 governs filing papers with the clerk, but does not provide for retention as a minute, delivery of an enforceable certified copy, or return of supporting documents.

correspondences.note_fr: L’ordonnance et la requête sont conservées au greffe comme minutes, avec conservation provisoire des pièces produites. La Rule 43.02 prévoit le dépôt des actes et autres documents auprès du greffier, mais ne règle pas expressément leur conservation comme minutes ni la garde provisoire des pièces.
correspondences.note_en: The order and petition are retained by the clerk as the court’s minute, with supporting documents held provisionally. Rule 43.02 governs filing pleadings and other papers with the clerk, but does not expressly address retention as minutes or provisional custody of supporting documents.

norms.heading: Time, Computation of – Extension – Service of Motions

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 44 — Time

norms.text:
(a) Computation. In computing any period of time prescribed or allowed by these rules, by order of court, or by any applicable statute, the day of the act, event, or default after which the designated period of time begins to run is not to be included. The last day of the period so computed is to be included, unless it is a Saturday, Sunday or a legal holiday, in which event the period runs until the end of the next day which is neither a Saturday, Sunday nor a legal holiday.
When the period of time prescribed or allowed is less than seven days, intermediate Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays shall be excluded in the computation.
(b) Enlargement.
When by these rules or by a notice given thereunder or by order of court an act is required or allowed to be done at or within a specified time, the court for cause shown may at any time in its discretion (1) with or without motion or notice order the period enlarged if request therefor is made before the expiration of the period originally prescribed or as extended by a previous order or (2) upon notice and motion made after the expiration of the specified period permit the act to be done where the failure to act was the result of excusable neglect;
but it may not extend the time for taking any action under Rules 52.13, 72.01, 73.01, 75.01, 78.04, 81.04, 81.07, and 84.035 or for commencing civil action.
(c) Motions – Notice Required – Affidavits. A written motion, other than one which may be heard ex parte, and notice of the hearing thereof shall be served not later than five days before the time specified for the hearing, unless a different period is fixed by law or court rule or by order of the court.
Such an order may for cause shown be made on ex parte application. When a motion is supported by an affidavit, the affidavit shall be served with the motion; and, except as otherwise provided by law or rule in connection with a motion for a new trial, opposing affidavits may be served not later than one day before the hearing, unless the court permits them to be served at some other time.
(d) Additional Time After Service by Mail. Whenever a party has the right or is required to do some act or take some proceedings within a prescribed period after the service of a notice or other paper upon the party and the notice or paper is served by mail, three days shall be added to the prescribed period.

correspondences.note_fr: Le CPC met à la charge des parties la conduite de l’instance et l’accomplissement des actes dans les formes et délais requis. La Rule 44.01 encadre les délais et actes de procédure, et la Rule 67.03 permet une dismissal pour défaut de prosecution ou de respect des règles ou ordonnances.
correspondences.note_en: The CPC places responsibility for conducting the action and performing procedural acts in the required form and time on the parties. Rule 44.01 addresses procedural time limits and acts, while Rule 67.03 permits dismissal for failure to prosecute or comply with rules or court orders.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 511 fixe le point de départ du délai de grâce selon le caractère contradictoire du jugement ou sa notification. La Rule 44.01 régit le calcul général des délais, tandis que la Rule 74.03 prévoit la notification de l’entrée du jugement, sans reprendre exactement cette distinction.
correspondences.note_en: Article 511 sets the starting point for the grace period depending on whether the judgment was adversarial or notified. Rule 44.01 provides general time-computation rules, while Rule 74.03 addresses notice of entry, without reproducing the same distinction.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 528 fixe le point de départ du délai de recours à la notification du jugement, sauf délai courant dès le jugement. Les Rules 81.04 et 81.05 organisent le délai d’appel à compter de la finalité du jugement, sans faire de la notification le point de départ général; Rule 44.01 concerne le calcul du délai.
correspondences.note_en: Article 528 starts the time for a remedy upon notification of the judgment, unless the law starts it on the judgment date. Rules 81.04 and 81.05 instead tie the appeal period to finality, not generally to notification; Rule 44.01 supplies computation rules.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article fixe comme point de départ la date de l’acte, de l’événement, de la décision ou de la notification génératrice du délai. Les textes du Missouri règlent la computation à partir de l’acte, de l’événement ou du défaut, mais ne mentionnent pas expressément la décision ou la notification.
correspondences.note_en: The article identifies the act, event, decision, or notification triggering the period as its starting point. Missouri provisions address computation from the act, event, or default, but do not expressly mention decisions or notifications.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article exclut le jour de départ et fixe des règles détaillées pour les délais en jours, mois et années. Les textes du Missouri excluent également le jour initial, mais ne prévoient pas les règles spécifiques de quantième pour les mois et les années et ajoutent une règle pour les délais de moins de sept jours.
correspondences.note_en: The article excludes the triggering day and provides detailed rules for periods expressed in days, months, and years. Missouri likewise excludes the initial day, but lacks the specific month-and-year anniversary rules and adds a rule for periods shorter than seven days.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article prévoit l’expiration à la fin du dernier jour et la prorogation lorsque celui-ci tombe un samedi, un dimanche ou un jour férié ou chômé. Les deux textes du Missouri prévoient substantiellement la même prorogation jusqu’à la fin du jour suivant non férié ni de week-end.
correspondences.note_en: The article provides that a period expires at the end of the last day and is extended when that day is a Saturday, Sunday, or holiday. Both Missouri provisions provide substantially the same extension until the end of the next non-weekend, non-holiday day.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article étend les règles de computation des délais aux inscriptions et formalités de publicité. Les règles 44.01 et RSMo 506.060 visent largement tout délai prévu par une règle, une ordonnance ou une loi, sans distinction selon la formalité concernée.
correspondences.note_en: The article extends general time-computation rules to registrations and other publication formalities. Rule 44.01 and RSMo 506.060 broadly cover any period prescribed by a rule, court order, or statute, without distinguishing the underlying procedural act.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 645 rend générales les prorogations de délais prévues par les articles 643 et 644, sous réserve des dérogations expresses, notamment en matière d’élections. La Rule 44.01(b), RSMo 512.140 et la Rule 81.20 permettent certaines extensions, mais dans des domaines et sous des conditions différentes, sans règle générale équivalente.
correspondences.note_en: Article 645 makes the extensions under Articles 643 and 644 generally applicable, subject to express exceptions, especially for election appeals. Rule 44.01(b), RSMo 512.140, and Rule 81.20 authorize extensions in specified contexts, but do not provide the same general rule or election-specific limitation.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article proroge au premier jour ouvrable le délai pour un acte électronique impossible à transmettre le dernier jour pour une cause étrangère à son auteur. Les règles du Missouri prévoient le report des échéances tombant un jour non ouvrable et, plus généralement, une prorogation judiciaire pour cause démontrée, mais pas cette prorogation automatique spécifique.
correspondences.note_en: The article extends the deadline to the next business day when an electronic filing cannot be transmitted on the last day for a cause external to the filer. Missouri rules defer deadlines falling on nonbusiness days and allow judicial enlargement for cause, but do not provide the same specific automatic extension.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 800 prévoit une clôture partielle liée au défaut d’accomplissement d’un acte, ainsi que sa rétractation pour des moyens nouveaux ou une cause grave. La règle 44.01 traite de l’extension des délais pour négligence excusable et la règle 74.06 de la remise en cause de certains jugements ou ordonnances, sans établir ce régime de clôture.
correspondences.note_en: Article 800 provides partial closure for failure to take a procedural step and permits retraction for new matters or good cause. Rule 44.01 addresses extensions for excusable neglect and Rule 74.06 relief from certain judgments or orders, but neither establishes this closure system.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 832 encadre une demande incidente de délai de paiement formée par courrier au greffe, avec communication des pièces et possibilité d’absence à l’audience. Les Rules 55.26, 43.01, 43.02 et 44.01 traitent respectivement de la forme des motions, de leur notification, du dépôt et du délai de notification, mais ne reproduisent pas ce régime particulier.
correspondences.note_en: Article 832 governs an incidental payment-time request filed by letter with the clerk, including transmission of supporting documents and the applicant’s possible nonappearance. Rules 55.26, 43.01, 43.02, and 44.01 address motion form, service, filing, and notice timing, but do not replicate this specific procedure.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article autorise une demande incidente de délai de paiement par requête remise ou adressée au greffe, avec information préalable de l’adversaire et pièces jointes. Les Rules 55.26 et 44.01 encadrent respectivement les demandes d’ordonnance par motion et la notification des motions, mais ne couvrent pas la requête au greffe ni les règles sur la non-comparution et les demandes formées contre la partie absente.
correspondences.note_en: The article permits an incidental payment-time request by petition filed with or sent to the clerk, with prior notice to the opponent and supporting documents. Rules 55.26 and 44.01 address applications for orders by motion and service of motions, but do not cover filing with the clerk or the rules on nonappearance and claims against an absent party.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 911 règle la notification et la signification des conclusions d’appel, les délais, leur prorogation et les sanctions, avec une exception en cas de force majeure. La Rule 43.01 encadre la signification aux avocats et parties, tandis que les Rules 44.01 et 84.05 prévoient certaines extensions de délais; aucune ne reprend l’ensemble du régime français.
correspondences.note_en: Article 911 governs service of appellate submissions, deadlines, extensions, sanctions, and relief for force majeure. Rule 43.01 addresses service on attorneys and parties, while Rules 44.01 and 84.05 provide limited mechanisms for extending deadlines; none reproduces the full French regime.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 912 organise l’examen de l’affaire, le calendrier de mise en état, la clôture, les plaidoiries et la radiation en cas d’inaction. La Rule 84.02 permet une conférence de mise au rôle et l’établissement d’un calendrier d’appel; les Rules 84.05, 44.01 et 84.08 couvrent seulement certains délais, extensions et défauts.
correspondences.note_en: Article 912 organizes case review, a case-management schedule, closure, argument, and dismissal for procedural inactivity. Rule 84.02 permits a docketing conference and scheduling in an appeal, while Rules 84.05, 44.01, and 84.08 address only portions of the timing, extension, and default consequences.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1031 impose au défendeur de signifier sous quinze jours s’il entend utiliser la pièce arguée de faux et prévoit, en cas d’affirmation ou de silence, le renvoi devant la juridiction désignée pour statuer sur le faux. Les Rules 43.01 et 44.01 régissent respectivement les modalités de signification et le calcul des délais, sans organiser cette procédure de faux ni le renvoi.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1031 requires the defendant, within fifteen days, to notify whether the allegedly forged document will be used and provides for referral to a designated court if the answer is affirmative or absent. Rules 43.01 and 44.01 cover service and time computation, but not the forgery proceeding or referral.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article prévoit une augmentation de certains délais par renvoi à l'article 1023. La Rule 44.01 permet le calcul de délais, l'ajout de trois jours en cas de notification postale et leur prorogation sous conditions, mais ne prévoit pas la même augmentation automatique.
correspondences.note_en: The article increases specified periods by reference to Article 1023. Rule 44.01 governs time computation, adds three days after service by mail, and permits extensions under conditions, but does not provide the same automatic increase.

correspondences.note_fr: La Rule 44.01 énonce des règles générales de calcul et de prolongation des délais procéduraux, mais ne prévoit ni l'opposition dans les quinze jours, ni la nouvelle convocation par le juge, ni la nouvelle délibération du conseil de famille.
correspondences.note_en: Rule 44.01 supplies general rules for computing and extending procedural periods, but does not establish the fifteen-day objection, the judge’s renewed-convocation duty, or the council’s renewed deliberation.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article accorde au ministère public un délai d'appel de quinze jours à compter de la remise de l'avis. La Rule 81.04 prévoit l'appel dans les dix jours suivant la finalité du jugement, tandis que la Rule 44.01 fixe les règles générales de computation des délais, sans règle spécifique au ministère public.
correspondences.note_en: The article gives the public prosecutor fifteen days to appeal from delivery of notice. Rule 81.04 allows an appeal within ten days after finality, and Rule 44.01 supplies general time-computation rules, but neither contains the article’s prosecutor-specific rule.

correspondences.note_fr: Le délai d'appel court, selon les destinataires, à compter de la notification ou de l'ordonnance. Le Missouri fixe en principe le délai à dix jours après que le jugement ou l'ordonnance est devenu définitif, avec des règles générales de computation, sans reprendre ce régime de notification.
correspondences.note_en: The appeal period runs, depending on the recipient, from notification or from the order. Missouri generally sets a ten-day period after the judgment or order becomes final, with general computation rules, but does not reproduce this notification-based scheme.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article permet au juge d’accorder, pour cause de complexité, une prorogation pouvant aller jusqu’à un an, sur demande du notaire ou d’un copartageant. La Rule 44.01 autorise également l’extension judiciaire d’un délai pour cause justifiée, mais selon un régime général et sans plafond ni procédure propres au partage successoral.
correspondences.note_en: The article permits the judge to extend the partition deadline, up to one year, because of complexity and upon request by the notary or a co-heir. Rule 44.01 likewise permits judicial enlargement for cause, but is a general rule without this specific one-year cap or partition procedure.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article fixe le délai d’opposition et son report lorsque la signification n’a pas été faite à personne, jusqu’à un acte ultérieur ou une mesure d’exécution. La Rule 55.25 fixe des délais de réponse après signification, tandis que la Rule 44.01 en règle le calcul, sans reprendre ce régime particulier.
correspondences.note_en: The article sets the opposition deadline and extends it when service was not personal until a later personal act or an enforcement measure. Rule 55.25 sets response deadlines after service, and Rule 44.01 governs computation, but neither reproduces this special regime.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose des délais spéciaux de décision et d’attente, ainsi qu’une intervention d’office du procureur. La Rule 44.01 peut régir le calcul de ces délais légaux, mais ne prévoit ni leurs durées particulières ni le rôle du procureur.
correspondences.note_en: The article imposes special decision and waiting periods and provides for ex officio action by the prosecutor. Rule 44.01 may govern computation of these statutory periods, but it supplies neither their specific durations nor the prosecutor’s role.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article fixe des délais spécifiques de saisine et de jugement, ainsi qu’une adaptation territoriale propre au droit français. La Rule 44.01 régit le calcul général des délais légaux, mais ne reprend pas ces délais ni cette adaptation territoriale.
correspondences.note_en: The article sets specific filing and decision deadlines and includes a territorial adaptation specific to French law. Rule 44.01 governs general computation of statutory periods but does not reproduce those deadlines or the territorial adaptation.

(a) A change of venue shall be ordered in a civil action triable by jury that is pending in a county having seventy-five thousand or less inhabitants upon the filing of a written application therefor not later than ten days after answer is due to be filed; except (1) in condemnation cases the application shall be filed not later than ten days after exceptions to the commissioner's report are filed and (2) in any civil action in which an answer is not required to be filed the application must be filed within ten days after the return date of the summons or order to show cause.

norms.heading: Change of Venue From Inhabitants for Cause – Procedure

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 51 — Venue, Including Change of Venue and Change of Judge

norms.text:
(a) A change of venue may be ordered in any civil action triable by jury for the following causes:

(1) That the inhabitants of the county are prejudiced against the applicant; or

(2) That the opposite party has an undue influence over the inhabitants of the county.

(b) The application for change of venue must be filed at least thirty days before the trial date or within ten days after a trial date is fixed, whichever date is later.
(c) A copy of the application and a notice of the time when it will be presented to the court must be served on all parties.

(d) The application shall set forth the cause or causes for the change of venue. It need not be verified and may be signed by the party or by an agent or attorney.
(e) The adverse party, within ten days after the filing of the application for change of venue, may file a denial of the cause or causes alleged in the application. Such denial may be signed by the party, an agent or attorney, and need not be verified. If a denial is filed, the court shall hear evidence and determine the issues.
If they are determined in favor of applicant, or if no denial is filed, a change of venue shall be ordered to some other county convenient to the parties and where the cause or causes do not exist. The court may enlarge the time for filing a denial as provided in Rule 44.01(b).

(f) Application for change of venue may be made by one or more parties in any of the following classes:
(1) plaintiffs;

(2) defendants;

(3) third-party plaintiffs (where a separate trial has been ordered);

(4) third-party defendants;

(5) intervenors.
Each of the foregoing classes is limited to one change of venue and any such change granted any one or more members of a class, including changes granted under Rules 51.02, 51.03 or 51.04, exhausts the right of all members of the class to a change of venue, with this exception: in condemnation cases involving multiple defendants, as to which separate trials are to be held, each such separate trial to determine damages shall be treated as a separate case for purposes of change of venue.
(g) When a change of venue is ordered, the entire civil action shall be removed, unless a separate trial has been ordered, in which event the court shall order removed only that part of the civil action in which applicant is involved.

norms.heading: Change of Judge – Procedure

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 51 — Venue, Including Change of Venue and Change of Judge

norms.text:
(a) A change of judge shall be ordered in any civil action upon the timely filing of a written application therefor by a party. For purposes of this Rule 51, proceedings to revoke probation or judicial parole and motions to modify child custody, child support, or spousal maintenance filed pursuant to chapter 452, RSMo, are not an independent action unless the judge designated to rule on the motion is not the same judge that ruled on the previous independent civil action. The application need not allege or prove any cause for such change of judge and need not be verified.
(b) The application must be filed within 60 days from service of process or 30 days from the designation of the trial judge, whichever time is longer. If the designation of the trial judge occurs less than thirty days before trial, the application must be filed prior to any appearance before the trial judge.

In the case of intervenors, the application must be filed within 30 days of intervention or designation of the trial judge, whichever is later, but in no event may any intervening party obtain a change of judge pursuant to this Rule 51 unless the application is filed within 180 days of the designation of the trial judge.
(c) A copy of the application and notice of the time when it will be presented to the court shall be served on all parties.

(d) Application for change of judge may be made by one or more parties in any of the following classes:

(1) plaintiffs;

(2) defendants;

(3) third-party plaintiffs (where a separate trial has been ordered);
(4) third-party defendants; or

(5) intervenors.

Each of the foregoing classes is limited to one change of judge, and any such change granted any one or more members of a class exhausts the right of all members of the class to a change of judge. However, no party shall be precluded from later requesting any change of judge for cause. Further, in condemnation cases involving multiple defendants, as to which separate trials are to be held, each separate trial to determine damages shall be treated as a separate case for purposes of change of judge.
(e) The judge promptly shall sustain a timely application for change of judge upon its presentation. The disqualified judge shall transfer the case to a judge stipulated to by the parties if the new judge agrees to take the case. If the case is not so transferred, the disqualified judge shall notify the presiding judge:

(1) If the presiding judge is not disqualified in the case, the presiding judge shall assign a judge of the circuit who is not disqualified or request this Court to transfer a judge; or
(2) If the presiding judge is disqualified in the case, a judge of the circuit shall be assigned in accordance with local court rules, so long as the local court rules do not permit the disqualified judge to make the assignment, or the presiding judge shall request this Court to transfer a judge.

(f) If after a change of judge has been granted the action shall be removed on application of another party to some other county in the same circuit, the transferred judge shall continue as the judge therein.

RSMo 508.090 et 508.140 organisent la disqualification et le changement de venue pour partialité ou influence, tandis que les Rules 51.04 et 51.05 prévoient respectivement le changement de venue ou de juge, avec des déclencheurs différents.
correspondences.note_en: The article permits transfer to a neighboring jurisdiction when a judge or legal officer is a party. RSMo 508.090 and 508.140 address disqualification and venue changes for prejudice or influence, while Rules 51.04 and 51.05 provide venue or judge changes on different grounds and procedures.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge qui estime devoir s’abstenir est remplacé par un autre juge désigné par le président de la juridiction. La Rule 51.07 impose au juge récusé de transférer l’affaire au président du circuit, selon la procédure de réaffectation de la Rule 51.05(e).
correspondences.note_en: A judge who believes recusal is warranted is replaced by another judge designated by the court’s presiding authority. Rule 51.07 requires a recused judge to transfer the case to the circuit’s presiding judge for reassignment under Rule 51.05(e).

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 342 impose de présenter la récusation ou le renvoi dès la connaissance de la cause et au plus tard avant la clôture des débats. Le RSMo 508.130 exige d’indiquer quand la cause a été connue, tandis que la Rule 51.05 fixe des délais pour le changement de juge, avec des conditions différentes.
correspondences.note_en: Article 342 requires recusal or transfer to be sought promptly after the grounds become known and no later than the close of argument. RSMo 508.130 requires the application to state when the grounds were discovered, while Rule 51.05 sets different deadlines for a change of judge.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 344 fixe l’autorité saisie, les modalités de dépôt, le contenu obligatoire de la demande et les pièces justificatives. Le RSMo 508.130 exige une requête exposant le motif, la date de sa découverte et un affidavit; la Rule 51.05 prévoit une demande écrite, mais sans motif ni vérification pour le changement de juge de droit.
correspondences.note_en: Article 344 specifies the deciding authority, filing method, required grounds, and supporting documents. RSMo 508.130 requires a petition stating the cause, when it was learned, and an affidavit; Rule 51.05 requires a written application but generally dispenses with cause and verification for a change of judge.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 345 organise l’information du juge, les observations, l’abstention et l’absence d’effet suspensif, avec une suspension possible ordonnée par le premier président. Le RSMo 508.140 prévoit un avis à la partie adverse et l’examen de la demande; la Rule 51.05 organise ensuite le transfert et la réattribution, sans mécanisme correspondant de sursis.
correspondences.note_en: Article 345 governs notice to the judge, observations, recusal, the absence of an automatic stay, and a possible stay ordered by the chief judge. RSMo 508.140 provides notice and consideration of the application; Rule 51.05 provides transfer and reassignment, but not the corresponding stay mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 346 règle la décision rapide sur la récusation ou le renvoi, l’avis de la décision et le pourvoi contre le rejet. La Rule 51.05(e) impose la prise en compte rapide d’une demande de changement de juge et la réattribution; le RSMo 508.140 prévoit l’examen de la demande, mais aucun délai ni recours correspondant n’est fourni.
correspondences.note_en: Article 346 governs prompt disposition, notice of the decision, and review of a denial. Rule 51.05(e) requires prompt action on a change-of-judge application and reassignment; RSMo 508.140 provides consideration of the application, but the supplied texts contain no matching deadline or appeal.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article prévoit le remplacement du juge récusé et le renvoi de l'affaire en cas de suspicion légitime, ainsi que des effets sur les actes et décisions antérieurs. Les Rules 51.07 et 51.05 organisent la réaffectation ou le changement de juge, mais ne reprennent pas tous ces effets.
correspondences.note_en: The article provides for replacement of a recused judge or transfer for legitimate suspicion, together with effects on prior acts and decisions. Rules 51.07 and 51.05 provide reassignment or change of judge, but do not reproduce all of those effects.

norms.heading: Transfer of Venue When Venue Improper

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 51 — Venue, Including Change of Venue and Change of Judge

norms.text:
(a) Any motion to transfer venue alleging improper venue shall be filed within 60 days of service on the party seeking transfer. For good cause shown, the court may extend the time to file a motion to transfer venue or allow the party to amend it. Any motion to transfer venue shall:

(1) Specify one or more counties in which the movant contends venue is proper, and
(2) State the basis for venue in each such county.

If a motion to transfer venue is not timely filed, the issue of improper venue is waived.

If a timely motion to transfer venue is filed, the venue issue is not waived by any other action in the case.

(b) Within 30 days after the filing of a motion to transfer for improper venue, an opposing party may file a reply. For good cause shown, the court may extend the time to file the reply or allow the party to amend it.
The reply shall state the basis for venue in the forum or state reasons why venue is not proper in one or more counties specified by the movant. The court shall not consider any basis not stated in the reply, nor shall the court consider allegations relating to fictitious defendants. If a reply is filed, the court may allow discovery on the issue of venue and shall determine the issue.
(c) If no reply is filed, the court shall order transfer to one of the counties specified in the motion. If a reply is filed but the issue is determined in favor of the movant, the court shall order a transfer of venue to a court where venue is proper. When a transfer of venue is ordered, the entire civil action shall be transferred unless a separate trial has been ordered. If a separate trial is ordered, only that part of the civil action in which the movant is involved shall be transferred.
(d) A request for transfer of venue under this Rule 51.045 shall not deprive a party of the right to a change of venue under Rule 51.03 if the civil action is transferred to a county having 75,000 or fewer inhabitants. A party seeking a change of venue under Rule 51.03, after transfer of venue pursuant to this Rule 51.045, shall make application therefor within the later of:
(1) The time allowed by Rule 51.03, or

(2) Ten days of being served with notice of the docketing of the civil action in the transferee court as provided by Rule 51.10.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article 75 impose que l'exception d'incompétence soit motivée et indique la juridiction demandée. La Rule 55.26 exige une motivation précise et le dispositif sollicité ; la Rule 51.045 impose, en matière de venue, d'indiquer les comtés et le fondement, mais ces textes ne couvrent pas exactement toute l'incompétence française.
correspondences.note_en: Article 75 requires the jurisdictional objection to state its grounds and identify the requested court. Rule 55.26 requires particular grounds and the relief sought; Rule 51.045 requires identifying proper counties and their basis for improper venue, but neither fully covers French jurisdictional objections.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article 77 autorise, dans certains cas, le relevé d'office de l'incompétence territoriale. La Rule 51.045 organise la demande de transfert pour improper venue, avec un délai et une renonciation ; RSMo 509.290 permet de soulever l'improper venue par motion ; RSMo 508.010 prévoit le transfert depuis un comté inapproprié, sans reprendre les distinctions françaises.
correspondences.note_en: Article 77 permits sua sponte territorial-jurisdiction review in specified proceedings. Rule 51.045 governs a motion to transfer for improper venue, including a deadline and waiver; RSMo 509.290 permits improper venue to be raised by motion; RSMo 508.010 provides transfer from an improper county without reproducing the French distinctions.

correspondences.note_fr: Le créancier peut demander par avance le renvoi de l'affaire devant la juridiction qu'il estime compétente en cas d'opposition. La Rule 51.045 organise le transfert pour mauvaise compétence territoriale, mais sur motion, dans des délais et selon des conditions différents.
correspondences.note_en: The creditor may ask in advance that, if opposition is filed, the matter be sent to the court the creditor considers competent. Rule 51.045 provides for transfer based on improper venue, but upon motion and under materially different timing and conditions.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article fixe des règles spéciales de compétence territoriale selon le lieu d’établissement de l’acte et le domicile du demandeur. RSMo 508.010 énonce des règles générales de venue, tandis que Rule 51.045 organise le transfert en cas de venue impropre, sans règle propre à la reconstitution d’actes.
correspondences.note_en: The article establishes special territorial rules based on where the instrument was made and where the claimant resides. RSMo 508.010 provides general venue rules, while Rule 51.045 governs transfer for improper venue; neither contains the article’s action-specific rules.

norms.heading: Civil Actions – In Whose Name Prosecuted – Suits in Representation Capacity – Civil Actions in Name of State – Real Property in Interest to Bring Civil Action

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 52 — Parties

norms.text: Every civil action shall be prosecuted in the name of the real party in interest, but an executor, administrator, guardian, trustee of an express trust, a party with whom or in whose name a contract has been made for the benefit of another and a party authorized by statute may sue in their own names in such representative capacity without joining the party for whose benefit the action is brought. When a statute so provides, a civil action for the use or benefit of another shall be brought in the name of the State of Missouri.

committee_notes:

This is substantially the same as prior Rule 52.01.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 31 ouvre l’action aux personnes ayant un intérêt légitime, sous réserve des qualités exigées par la loi. Les Rule 52.01 et RSMo 507.010 imposent que l’action soit engagée par la real party in interest, sans énoncer la règle générale française ni ses exceptions.
correspondences.note_en: Article 31 permits actions by persons with a legitimate interest, subject to statutory qualifications. Rule 52.01 and RSMo 507.010 require prosecution by the real party in interest, but do not state the broader French rule or its exceptions.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 32 rend irrecevable la prétention formée par ou contre une personne dépourvue du droit d’agir. Rule 55.27 permet de soulever l’absence de capacité juridique, et Rule 52.01 ainsi que RSMo 507.010 exigent que l’action soit engagée par la real party in interest, mais ces textes ne recouvrent pas exactement toute la notion française de droit d’agir.
correspondences.note_en: Article 32 makes a claim inadmissible when brought by or against a person lacking the right to sue or be sued. Rule 55.27 permits an objection based on lack of legal capacity, while Rule 52.01 and RSMo 507.010 require the real party in interest; these provisions do not fully match the broader French concept.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 414 limite la représentation d’une partie à une seule personne habilitée par la loi. Les textes du Missouri autorisent certaines personnes à agir en qualité représentative sans joindre le bénéficiaire, mais ne posent pas cette limitation générale à un seul représentant.
correspondences.note_en: Article 414 limits a party to representation by one person legally authorized to act. Missouri permits specified persons to sue in a representative capacity without joining the beneficiary, but does not impose the same general one-representative limit.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 421 permet au ministère public d’agir comme partie principale, d’intervenir comme partie jointe et de représenter autrui dans les cas prévus par la loi. Les Rules 52.12 et 52.01 traitent respectivement de l’intervention et de l’action en représentation, tandis que la Rule 98.02 prévoit spécialement l’action du procureur au nom de l’État en quo warranto, sans énoncer la règle générale française.
correspondences.note_en: Article 421 permits the public prosecutor to act as a principal party, intervene as a joined party, and represent others where authorized by law. Rules 52.12 and 52.01 address intervention and representative actions, while Rule 98.02 specifically permits prosecutors to proceed in the State’s name in quo warranto, but none states the French general rule.

frcp.evidence: Committee Note – 1974 Paragraph (a) is the same as Rule 24(a) of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1049 ouvre l’action à toute personne intéressée et au ministère public. RSMo 507.010 et la Rule 52.01 exigent en principe l’action du véritable intéressé, tout en admettant certaines actions représentatives ou autorisées par la loi, sans prévoir expressément le ministère public.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1049 allows any interested person and the public prosecutor to bring the action. RSMo 507.010 and Rule 52.01 generally require prosecution by the real party in interest, while permitting specified representative or statutory actions, but do not expressly provide for a public prosecutor.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article autorise certaines associations de lutte contre les discriminations à agir pour la victime, sous réserve d’un accord écrit détaillé, et permet à la victime d’intervenir ou de mettre fin à l’instance. La Rule 52.01 reconnaît l’action représentative autorisée par la loi, tandis que les Rules 52.12 et 52.08 encadrent respectivement l’intervention et les actions représentatives collectives, sans ces conditions spécifiques.
correspondences.note_en: The article permits qualifying anti-discrimination associations to sue for a victim subject to detailed written consent, while allowing the victim to intervene or terminate the proceeding. Rule 52.01 recognizes statutory representative standing; Rules 52.12 and 52.08 address intervention and representative class actions, but do not impose these specific conditions.

norms.heading: Civil Actions By and Against Minors and Mentally or Physically Infirm

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 52 — Parties

norms.text:
(a) Civil Actions by Minors, Prosecuted by Whom. Civil actions by minors may be commenced and prosecuted only by a duly appointed guardian of such minor or, if there is no such guardian, by a next friend appointed in such civil action; if asserted by counterclaim, cross-claim or third party pleadings, such civil action may only be prosecuted by a duly appointed guardian of such minor or, if there is no such guardian, by a guardian ad litem appointed for such civil action.
(b) Next Friend, by Whom Appointed. The appointment of a next friend for a minor shall be made by the judge of the court in which the civil action is intended to be brought, or by the clerk thereof.
(c) How Appointed. Such appointment shall be made on the petition in writing of such minor if of the age of fourteen years and the written consent of the person proposed to be next friend. If such minor be under the age of fourteen years, the appointment of a next friend may be made upon the written application of a relative or friend of the minor, in which case a notice thereof must be given to the person with whom such minor resides.
(d) Petition and Appointment to be Filed Before Further Proceedings. The petition for the appointment of a next friend, the written consent of the person proposed to be next friend, and the order of appointment, shall be filed in the office of the clerk of the court where the civil action is proposed to be brought before any proceedings shall be had in the cause.
(e) Civil Actions Against Minors Not to Proceed Without Guardian. After the commencement of a civil action against a minor defendant, and the service of process upon him, the civil action shall not be prosecuted any further until a guardian or guardian ad litem for such minor defendant be appointed, except for such discovery proceedings as may be necessary to determine whether a defendant is a minor or has a duly appointed guardian.
(f) Appointment of Guardian Ad Litem. The appointment of a guardian ad litem shall be made by the court in which the civil action is pending upon the written request of the minor defendant, if of the age of fourteen years or more, or, if such minor be under said age, on the written request of a relative or friend of the minor, and on the written consent of any competent person proposed as guardian ad litem. Such request shall be filed in the office of the clerk of the court before any answer by such minor shall be filed.
(g) Guardian Ad Litem, When Appointed. If such minor defendant neglect, for one day after the expiration of the time within which the minor defendant is summoned to appear to the suit to procure the appointment of a guardian ad litem to defend the civil action, the court shall appoint some competent person to be guardian ad litem for such minor in the defense of such civil action.
(h) Next Friend or Guardian Ad Litem to Give Bond.

1. Before a next friend or guardian ad litem can receive a receipt for any money or property, personal or real, and before the next friend or guardian ad litem can acknowledge satisfaction or discharge of any judgment, the next friend or guardian ad litem must execute a bond to such minor; except that no bond shall be required if:
(i) the total value of the property or money, exclusive of expenses and fees approved by the court, is not in excess of ten thousand dollars and all of the money or property is to be turned over to the minor or the minor's parent or
(ii) a sufficiently bonded guardian files a receipt approved by the court for such money or property. The bond must be approved by the court and shall be conditioned that the next friend or guardian ad litem shall account to such minor for all money or property of such minor that has or does come into the next friend or guardian ad litem's hands, less only those expenses and attorney fees the payment of which has been approved by order of the court.
The bond shall be in an amount equal to the value of said money or property if the surety is a corporate bonding, surety or insurance company and in an amount double the value of said money or property if the surety is not a corporate bonding, surety or insurance company, in which event there shall be two sureties. In either event, the surety or sureties shall be approved by the court before the bond can be approved.
2. Failure to execute such approved bond with approved surety or sureties when required under the provisions of subsection 1 shall, upon receipt by a next friend or guardian ad litem of any money or property for or on behalf of such minor, immediately render such next friend or guardian ad litem personally liable to such minor for a penal sum in an amount double the value of such money or property and also shall render absolutely void and of no effect any release, receipt or acknowledgment of satisfaction or discharge of any judgment which has been or is in the future made or executed by the next friend or guardian ad litem.
3. The duties of the next friend or guardian ad litem and the obligations under such bond shall continue until discharged by order of the court.

(i) Guardian and Next Friend Liable for Costs. The guardian or next friend of any minor who commences or prosecutes a civil action shall be responsible for the costs thereof, unless such minor be permitted by the court to sue as a poor person, as provided by law.
(j) Guardian Ad Litem Liable for Costs in Case of Misconduct. No person appointed guardian ad litem for a minor, for the purpose of defending a civil action against such minor, shall be personally liable for the costs of such civil action, unless specially charged by the order of the court for some personal misconduct in said cause.
(k) Next Friend or Guardian Ad Litem for Mentally or Physically Infirm. Whenever it shall be suggested or affirmatively appear to the court that any person not having a duly appointed guardian is incapable by reason of mental or physical infirmity of instituting suit or of properly caring for the person's own interests in any litigation brought by or against such person, the court shall inquire into the person's mental or physical condition for the purpose of the particular litigation and shall hear and determine such issue.
If it is found to be proper for the protection of the person, the court may appoint a next friend or guardian ad litem for said person for the purpose of the particular litigation.

(l) Next Friend to Defend Counterclaim. A next friend shall also defend any counterclaim asserted against such minor or mentally or physically infirm person, except, upon application, the court shall appoint a guardian ad litem to defend such counterclaim.
(m) Failure to Appoint Next Friend or Guardian Ad Litem. Failure to appoint a next friend or guardian ad litem for a minor or a mentally or physically infirm person shall not invalidate the proceedings if the court finds that the interests of the minor or the mentally or physically infirm person were adequately protected.
(n) Statutes Governing Powers and Duties. The powers and duties of the next friend, guardian and guardian ad litem, and of the courts in respect to minors and incompetents shall be exercised in accordance with the provisions of the Revised Statutes of Missouri including, but not limited to, Sections 507.182, 507.184, 507.186 and 507.188.

correspondences.note_fr: La Rule 55.13 traite de la capacité et de l’autorité d’une partie ; la Rule 55.27 permet d’invoquer le défaut de capacité du demandeur ; la Rule 52.02 organise la représentation des mineurs et personnes infirmes. L’ensemble ne couvre pas exactement toutes les hypothèses françaises.
correspondences.note_en: Rule 55.13 addresses a party’s capacity and authority; Rule 55.27 permits a challenge based on the plaintiff’s lack of legal capacity; and Rule 52.02 governs representation of minors and infirm persons. Together, they do not exactly cover every French category.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge peut entendre les mineurs, majeurs protégés, représentants de personnes morales et agents ou membres de celles-ci. La Rule 57.03(b)(4) prévoit la désignation de représentants d’une organisation pour une déposition, tandis que la Rule 52.02 et le RSMo 510.020 concernent respectivement la représentation des personnes vulnérables et l’interrogatoire des parties ou sociétés.
correspondences.note_en: The judge may examine minors, protected adults, representatives of legal entities, and their members or agents. Rule 57.03(b)(4) provides for organizational representatives to testify by deposition, while Rule 52.02 and RSMo 510.020 address representation of vulnerable persons and interrogatories to parties or entities.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 369 prévoit plusieurs causes d’interruption automatique, dont la majorité et certains jugements d’insolvabilité. Les textes du Missouri traitent de la capacité et de la représentation des mineurs, ainsi que d’un sursis lié à la désignation d’un receiver, sans reprendre cette règle d’interruption automatique ni la cessation de fonctions de l’avocat.
correspondences.note_en: Article 369 provides several grounds for automatic interruption, including attaining majority and certain insolvency judgments. The Missouri texts address capacity and representation of minors and a receiver-related stay, but do not reproduce the automatic interruption rule or interruption caused by loss of counsel.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 370 prévoit l’interruption, après notification, en cas de décès transmissible, de cessation du représentant légal ou de modification de la capacité d’ester. Les règles 52.13 et RSMo 507.100 organisent plutôt la substitution ou la continuation de l’instance, avec motion et délais; Rule 52.02 encadre la représentation des mineurs.
correspondences.note_en: Article 370 interrupts the action, after notice, for a transmissible death, loss of a legal representative, or a change in capacity to litigate. Rule 52.13 and RSMo 507.100 instead provide for substitution or continuation by motion and subject to deadlines; Rule 52.02 governs minor representation.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article renvoie, pour la formation, l’instruction et le jugement, aux règles de la tutelle des majeurs. La Rule 52.02 prévoit seulement certaines règles de représentation en justice des mineurs ou personnes mentalement ou physiquement infirmes, et non une procédure complète de tutelle.
correspondences.note_en: The article applies the procedural rules governing adult guardianship to the application. Rule 52.02 provides only selected litigation-representation rules for minors and mentally or physically infirm persons, not a complete guardianship procedure.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article encadre la requête d’un époux face à l’impossibilité de volonté de l’autre, avec justificatifs, instruction et audition sauf dispense médicale. RSMo 451.300 prévoit une intervention judiciaire pour les actes concernant un conjoint incapable, tandis que Rule 52.02 prévoit l’examen judiciaire de l’infirmité, mais dans le cadre d’un litige.
correspondences.note_en: The article regulates a spouse’s application when the other spouse cannot express a will, requiring supporting evidence, possible investigation, and a hearing subject to medical waiver. RSMo 451.300 provides court-supervised action involving a disabled spouse, while Rule 52.02 addresses judicial inquiry into infirmity in litigation.

correspondences.note_fr: Le texte français exige une information du mineur sur son droit d’être entendu et assisté, à peine d’impossibilité d’homologation ou d’apposition de la formule exécutoire. Les textes du Missouri prévoient une représentation procédurale du mineur, l’examen de l’intérêt des enfants en médiation et l’approbation d’accords familiaux, sans imposer ces mêmes conditions.
correspondences.note_en: The French provision requires notice of the minor’s rights to be heard and assisted, barring approval or enforcement-form attachment if omitted. Missouri provisions address minor representation, children’s best interests in mediation, and approval of family agreements, but do not impose the same conditions.

norms.heading: Parties to Civil Action When Claim for Relief Accrues Under Law of Another State – Proceeds, How Distributed

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 52 — Parties

norms.text:
(a) Civil Action – By Whom Brought. Whenever a claim exists under the law of another state, a civil action thereon may be brought in this state by:

(1) the persons entitled to the proceeds of such claim if they are authorized to bring such action by the laws of said other state;

(2) the executor, administrator, guardian, guardian ad litem or other person empowered by the law of said other state to sue in a representative capacity if the persons entitled to the proceeds of such claim are not authorized to sue in such cases under the law of said other state.

(b) Proceeds – How Distributed. In the cases mentioned in subsection (a)(2) above, the proceeds of the civil action, resulting either from judgment or settlement, shall be paid to the person bringing such civil action and such person is authorized to satisfy the judgment and execute a release. Such person to whom the proceeds are paid shall have authority to distribute and pay the same to the person or persons entitled thereto, according to their respective interests therein, under the laws of said other state.

norms.heading: Joinder of Persons Needed for Just Adjudication

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 52 — Parties

norms.text:
(a) Persons to Be Joined if Feasible. A person shall be joined in the action if:

(1) in the person's absence complete relief cannot be accorded among those already parties, or

(2) the person claims an interest relating to the subject of the action and is so situated that the disposition of the action in the person's absence may:
(i) as a practical matter impair or impede the person's ability to protect that interest or

(ii) leave any of the persons already parties subject to a substantial risk of incurring double, multiple, or otherwise inconsistent obligations by reason of the claimed interest.

If the person has not been joined, the court shall order that the person be made a party. If the person should join as a plaintiff but refuses to do so, the person may be made a defendant.
(b) Determination by Court Whenever Joinder Not Feasible. If a person as described in Rule 52.04(a)(1) or Rule 52.04(a)(2) cannot be made a party, the court shall determine whether in equity and good conscience the action should proceed among the parties before it or should be dismissed, the absent party being thus regarded as indispensable. The factors to be considered by the court include:
(i) to what extent a judgment rendered in the person's absence might be prejudicial to that person or those already parties;

(ii) the extent to which by protective provisions in the judgment, by the shaping of relief, or other measures, the prejudice can be lessened or avoided;

(iii) whether a judgment rendered in the person's absence will be adequate; and
(iv) whether the plaintiff will have an adequate remedy if the action is dismissed for nonjoinder.

(c) Pleading Reasons for Nonjoinder. A pleading asserting a claim for relief shall state the names, if known to the pleader, of any persons as described in subdivisions (a)(1)-(2) hereof who are not joined, and the reasons why they are not joined.
(d) Exception of Class Actions. This rule is subject to the provisions of Rule 52.08.

norms.heading: Who may Join as Plaintiff and Defendant – Protective Orders, When

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 52 — Parties

norms.text:
(a) Permissive Joinder. All persons may join in one action as plaintiffs if they assert any right to relief jointly, severally, or in the alternative in respect of or arising out of the same transaction, occurrence or series of transactions or occurrences and if any question of law or fact common to all of them will arise in the action.
All persons may be joined in one action as defendants if there is asserted against them jointly, severally, or in the alternative, any right to relief in respect of or arising out of the same transaction, occurrences or series of transactions or occurrences and if any question of law or fact common to all of them will arise in the action. A plaintiff or defendant need not be interested in obtaining or defending against all the relief demanded. Judgment may be given for one or more of the plaintiffs according to their respective rights to relief, and against one or more defendants according to their respective liabilities.
(b) Separate Trials – Protective Orders. The court may make such orders as will prevent a party from being embarrassed, delayed, or put to expense by the inclusion of a person as a party against whom the party asserts no claim and the person asserts no claim against the party and may order separate trials or make other orders to prevent delay or prejudice.

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure

norms.text: Misjoinder of parties is not ground for dismissal of an action. Parties may be dropped or added by order of the court on motion of any party or of its own initiative at any stage of the action and on such terms as are just. Any claim against a party may be severed and proceeded with separately.
